title: Seminar · Find two explanations for the same recorded day
question: If the museum supplies a dozen more days with the same two durations and no scanner queue, which line of the candidate remains untested?
answer: When every object arrives at scanning after the scanner is free, starting at inspection completion always happens to work. Those days cannot show whether the candidate waits for an occupied scanner. Choose a change that makes the second object finish inspection while the first is still scanning.

title: Seminar · Write the expected outcome before running the change
question: The candidate gives 14 instead of 16 but passes the one-object control. What conclusion can this comparison support?
answer: It omits two minutes on the changed two-object question. Passing the one-object case is consistent with a defect that appears when scans overlap. Inspect the candidate’s per-object start times to distinguish an early start from another error that happens to produce the same finish time.

title: Seminar · Locate the first impossible event
question: Why include the case where scanning takes exactly four minutes? Which event first violates the scheduling rule at five minutes?
answer: At four minutes the second scan may begin exactly when the first one ends, so equality is allowed. At five minutes the first scan finishes at minute 9, but the candidate starts the second at minute 8. Its first impossible event is the second scan start. Renaming both objects leaves that event unchanged.

title: Independent task
question: The museum now asks about three objects. First all scans take three minutes. Next, only the middle scan takes seven. Finally move that longer duration to the last object. Before executing code, list the expected scan finishes in each case. Find the first impossible event in the candidate’s changed run and explain the value of moving the delay.
answer:
plans = {"original": [3, 3, 3], "middle delay": [3, 7, 3],
         "last delay": [3, 3, 7]}
# Independent expected finishes, calculated before running either rule.
expected = {"original": [7, 11, 15], "middle delay": [7, 15, 18],
            "last delay": [7, 11, 19]}
for case, scans in plans.items():
    scanner_free = 0
    replay = []
    shortcut = []
    for inspected, duration in zip([4, 8, 12], scans):
        shortcut.append(inspected + duration)
        scanner_free = max(inspected, scanner_free) + duration
        replay.append(scanner_free)
    print(case, "candidate", shortcut, "checked", replay)
    assert replay == expected[case]
original candidate [7, 11, 15] checked [7, 11, 15]
middle delay candidate [7, 15, 15] checked [7, 15, 18]
last delay candidate [7, 11, 19] checked [7, 11, 19]
The shortcut prints [7, 15, 15] for the middle delay. It starts the third scan at 12, three minutes before the scanner is free. The independently checked schedule ends at 18. Moving the delay to the last object leaves the first two finishes unchanged, and both rules end at 19. This control helps locate a waiting-time error in the middle-delay case.
